newsitem.title: UK: London freight - BFI down again but BIFFEX bounces.
newsitem.headline: London freight - BFI down again but BIFFEX bounces.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) fell another 11 points to 1,281, due to continued weakness in the Pacific, and a scarcity of fresh fixing in the Atlantic.
However, BIFFEX futures bounced on the back of expectations of firmer rates in the Atlantic following an increase in enquiry for that area on Thursday.
At the close, BIFFEX futures were 25 to 45 points firmer. Most active July traded last at 1,200, up 40 points. July volume ammounted to 85 lots, while total volume was 172 lots.
"I think BIFFEX was due a bounce having fallen so far recently," one trader said.
The Pacific sector still looks very weak, brokers said.

Little fresh grain fixing was seen from the U.S. Atlantic region. One though was Bunge's fixing of 2.747 million cubic feet of grain Mississippi/Rotterdam May 1-8 for a $635,000 lumpsum, which equates to $11.33 basis heavy grain.
On the mineral sector, coal and ore rates continued to look reasonably steady, brokers said.
Ankerkolen fixed 115,000 tonnes of coal Richards Bay/Rotterdam June 15-30 at $6.75, while on the ore side of the market, Rohstoffhandel fixed 220,000 tonnes ore Tubarao to Rotterdam May at $5.30.
The timecharter sector saw just the one new capesize fixture, which was the Irenes Vision 145,177 dwt del Antwerp May 18 trip transatlantic r/v for $12,000 daily by Cetragpa.

Panamax business saw Startrans take the Pcific Orient 67,478 del Nagoya spot for 12 months trading at $10,200 daily, while Daiichi took the Tomis Faith 65,362 dwt del Goa May 1-7 trip and redel Japan for $8,800 daily plus a $115,000 ballast bonus.
